appendix_title: FORMS OF VIṢṆU AS LETTERS OF THE ALPHABET (According to Tantra-sāra-saṁgraha)
content:

(According to Tantra-sāra-saṁgraha)

द्विरष्टपञ्चकचतुः पञ्चेत्येवाष्टवर्गगाः (१, ६)

summary: This appendix lists 51 forms of the Hindu deity Viṣṇu, with each form corresponding to one of the 51 letters of the Sanskrit alphabet. The list is sourced from the 'Tantra-sāra-saṁgraha'. The forms are organized into eight sections (vargas) which represent the constituent parts of the sacred syllable Oṁ (Aum) — a, u, m — followed by subsequent subtle spiritual states: Nāda, Bindu, Kalā, Śānta, and Ati-śānta. A Sanskrit verse at the beginning appears to describe the grouping of these letters.
purpose: The purpose of this appendix is to provide a reference list correlating the 51 letters of the Sanskrit alphabet (mātṛkā) with specific forms of Viṣṇu, as prescribed in the Tantric text, 'Tantra-sāra-saṁgraha'. This mapping is significant for meditational practices, mantra recitation, and rituals within certain Vaishnava and Tantric traditions, where each letter is considered a divine emanation or power.
key_information: The appendix provides a list of 51 forms of Viṣṇu corresponding to the 51 letters of the Sanskrit alphabet.
The primary source for this classification is cited as the 'Tantra-sāra-saṁgraha'.
The letters and their corresponding Viṣṇu forms are divided into eight groups or 'vargas'.
The first three groups are the components of Oṁkāra: 'अ' (vowels), 'उ' (k-varga), and 'म' (c-varga).
The remaining five groups are Nāda, Bindu, Kalā, Śānta, and Ati-śānta, representing progressively subtle stages of sound and consciousness.
The list for the first group (vowels) is incomplete, as it omits the 8th form, which would correspond to the long vowel ॠ (Ṝ).
A Sanskrit verse, 'द्विरष्टपञ्चकचतुः पञ्चेत्येवाष्टवर्गगाः (१, ६)', is included, likely referencing the structure of these eight groups.

tables_and_data.description: A comprehensive list of 51 forms of Viṣṇu, categorized into eight sections, each corresponding to a letter of the Sanskrit alphabet.
tables_and_data.data_summary: The data is a numbered list from 1 to 51 (with number 8 missing) that assigns a specific name of Viṣṇu to each letter. The list is structured into eight sections: I. The First Unit of Oṁkāra (अ) [16 forms, for the vowels]; II. The Second unit of Oṁkāra (उ) [5 forms, k-varga]; III. The Third unit of Oṁkāra (म) [5 forms, c-varga]; IV. Nāda [5 forms, ṭ-varga]; V. Bindu [5 forms, t-varga]; VI. Kalā [5 forms, p-varga]; VII. Śānta [4 forms, semi-vowels]; VIII. Ati-śānta [6 forms, sibilants and conjunct]. The list begins with '1. अजः' and concludes with '51. क्ष नृसिंहः'.

references_to_chapters: The citation '(१, ६)' following the Sanskrit verse likely refers to chapter 1, verse 6 of the 'Tantra-sāra-saṁgraha'.
